newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: VOLKSWAGEN SLOVAK UNIT REVISES UP '97 OUTPUT FORECAST.
newsitem.headline: VOLKSWAGEN SLOVAK UNIT REVISES UP '97 OUTPUT FORECAST.

text.p: Volkswagen Bratislava s.r.o., the Slovak unit of German car maker Volkswagen AG , has revised its 1997 output forecast to 34,000 cars, from an original estimate of 29,000, a company spokeswoman said.
"The original plan has been adjusted to 34,000 cars in 1997, based on the impressive production results over the first four months of the year," Maria Kovacikova told Reuters on Tuesday.
"We increased also our plan in production of gear boxes, to 281,000 from 268,400," Kovacikova said.
She said production at the plant, in financial terms, will rise by some two billion crowns to over 20 billion in total.
Originally, Volkswagen Bratislava planned to keep 1997 output at 1996 levels, when 30,147 cars were produced.

She said the plant will start to produce a new model -- the VW Passat B2 -- at the beginning of June, with planned output of about 4,000 cars to the end of the year. The unit's main production remains a variety of the VW Golf model.
In 1996, Slovak VW assembled 5,156 units of the Golf A3 Syncro model, 5,681 Golf Variant Syncro, 3,421 Passats and 15,889 units of the Golf A3.
Volskwagen AG originally took a stake in Bratislavske Automobilove Zavody (BAZ) in 1992, and became its sole owner acquiring the remaining 20 percent shares of BAZ in December 1995.
VW Bratislava employs some 950 people who assemble cars from kits imported from Germany. Volkswagen's investment into the plant between 1992 and 1994 totalled 130 million marks.

The factory exports roughly 95 percent of its production, mainly to western Europe. Last May, VW started production at a second plant in Slovakia, making car cabling systems in Nitra, 90 km (60 miles) east of Bratislava.
The venture, Volkswagen Elektricke Systemy s.r.o. supplies car cabling systems to VW group plants as well as to other car maufacturers.
